transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve come in because I’m having real trouble staying focused on work. I’ll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document fully intending to get through it, and then after about ten minutes I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page, thinking about three other things, and not really taking anything in. It’s frustrating.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?
Not really sure. I mean, I might shift around in my chair like anyone, but I haven’t noticed feeling especially restless or needing to move all the time.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

I don’t think so. I’m not usually the kind of person who does things on the spur of the moment. I might make the odd quick decision like anyone, but I wouldn’t say acting without thinking is a big issue for me.
Do you have trouble organizing tasks and activities?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think organizing is the main problem for me, or at least I haven’t noticed it as clearly. I can usually set things up and know what needs doing, but I’d have to think about whether I’m missing something there.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?
I’m not sure, honestly. I do get sidetracked sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than other people. I haven’t really paid close attention to what’s distracting me around me.
Do you have difficulty keeping your workspace or living space organized?
I’m not sure. I mean, my space can get a bit messy at times, like anyone’s, but I haven’t really thought of it as a major problem or something I consistently struggle with.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?
I don’t think so, not often. I might jump in occasionally if I’m excited or worried I’ll forget what I was going to say, but I haven’t noticed it being a regular issue.
Do you often find that you have trouble completing tasks because your mind wanders?

Yes, that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I’ll sit down with a stack of essays to mark or a curriculum document to work through, fully intending to get it done, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page. My mind’s gone off to three other things, and I’ve barely taken in what’s in front of me.
Are your difficulties with focus and staying on task causing problems for you at work or in your relationships?

Yes. At work it’s become a real issue. I’ve missed following through on things enough that my department chair has put me on a support plan, which is pretty embarrassing.

And at home, my wife has started taking over the bills and reminders, because she doesn’t really trust that I’ll keep track of them reliably. So yeah, it’s definitely affecting both.
Have you noticed any significant difficulties with learning new information?

I’m not sure I’d say learning new information is a major problem on its own. If it’s explained clearly and I can focus on it, I usually understand it. The trouble is more that sometimes I don’t take it in properly the first time, so I may need to reread things or have them repeated.
Have you experienced difficulties with focus and staying on task since childhood?

Yes, I think so. Even in primary school, my reports would say things like I was “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was watching me closely.

My parents also used to find worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d just forgotten to hand in. So it does feel like it’s been there a long time, not just something recent.
Do you often feel fidgety or restless when you're sitting still for a long period of time?
Not really, no. I mean, I might shift around a bit if I’m uncomfortable or in a long meeting, but I don’t usually feel especially restless or like I have to get up and move.
Do you often feel like you're 'on the go' or like you're 'driven by a motor'?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not usually someone who feels like I’m constantly moving or “driven by a motor.” I can sit still when I need to.
Do you often feel impatient when waiting for things?
Not especially. I can get a bit annoyed if something is taking ages, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say impatience with waiting is a big problem for me.
Do you think your main problem is with paying attention to details and making careless mistakes?
I’m not really sure. I do make mistakes sometimes, but I haven’t clearly noticed that it’s specifically because I’m not paying attention to details. I’d have to think about it a bit.
Do you think your main difficulty is with staying focused on what you're doing?

Yes, I think that’s probably the main thing. I’ll sit down with essays to mark or a curriculum document, fully intending to get through it, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page. My mind’s gone off to three other things, and I haven’t really taken in what’s in front of me.
Do you often have difficulty with self-regulation of emotions?
I’m not sure, really. I don’t think I’m someone who has big emotional outbursts or anything like that. I can get frustrated or irritated at times, but I haven’t noticed it as a main issue for me.
Do you often feel like you have excess energy?
Not really, no. I wouldn’t say I feel like I’ve got lots of extra energy. If anything, I’m more likely to feel mentally restless than physically energetic, but I’m not sure that’s what you mean.
Did you have any diagnoses or concerns about attention or behavior when you were a child?

Not a formal diagnosis, no. But there were definitely comments from school. Even in primary school, my reports would say things like I was “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping an eye on me. My parents also used to find worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d done but forgotten to hand in.
Have your difficulties with focus and staying on task caused problems in your friendships or social relationships outside of work?

Outside of work, yes, mainly at home. My wife has had to start taking over bills and reminders because she says she can’t rely on me to keep track of them. It’s caused some tension because I’ll mean to follow through, but then I don’t, and she ends up having to pick it up.

At work it’s become a bigger issue too — my department chair has put me on a support plan because of missed follow-through.
